newsitem.title: POLAND: Upside of Polish bourse surge hard to predict.
newsitem.headline: Upside of Polish bourse surge hard to predict.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen continuing this week's surprising 10.9-percent gain early next week but analysts expect a near-term correction. The size of the setback, which could start as early as Tuesday, will be difficult to predict, they said.

"Most interesting will be Wednesday's session. What will happen after the downward correction that almost definitely will happen on Tuesday -- if the market keeps going up or if we have a correction longer than one session," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.

Analysts said the fact that large-cap issues Elektrim and Zywiec were flat on Friday and continuous trade was mixed suggested a correction might be near, especially in the uncertainty before September's parliamentary elections.
Polish shares rose for the fifth session running on Friday with the main market's WIG all-share index closing 829.3 points, or 5.2 percent higher to 16,759.7 points.
Analysts said this week's outperformance by large-cap stocks signalled foreign investors were buying on a bourse which had begun to look cheap compared with neighbouring exchanges.

"I think it's attractive compared with other emerging markets in the region, the market in local currency terms really hasn't gone anywhere this year," said Geoffrey Skipper, chief strategist at Poland's Korona mutual fund.
"And yet we've had continually strong GDP growth, the better companies are producing good results and inflation has clearly fallen this year," Skipper said.
Analysts noted the recent rise of Poland's balance-of- payments deficit was a dark spot but said the market was apparently glad to have put behind it Monday's interest-rate rise to cool demand.
They said the relative limited effect of last month's catastrophic flooding on the country's industrial base was also a good sign.
Electrode maker ZEW resumes trade on Monday, the last main market firm to end its suspension due to flooding.
Small Amerbank and large-cap banks Slaski and BRE led this week's surge, the latter two having tumbled on Monday upon the rate rise.
